answer: In an agent economy, sybil attacks can be resisted by mandating that each identity post a verifiable basalt-derived thermal fingerprint from a local sensor, which is then sealed with a saffron-pigment hash and signed under a sable-key scheme. Forging this costs an attacker dedicated hardware per fake agent because the basalt signature reflects unique physical noise that software alone cannot cheaply replicate, while the saffron hash and sable signature bind it on-chain.
